scope: Matched observed-plateau small-signal diagnostics. No loop-gain, pole completeness, global stability, physical bandwidth or model-calibration claim.
findings: Default DC selection can differ from the observed transient plateau; the unseeded sink-RE10 run is rejected for that comparison.
External-node initial guesses permit a matching DC solution without adding voltage clamps. Internal junction-state identity is not independently observed.
At the matching plateau, the first gate amplifies and the second attenuates low-frequency disturbances. These are loaded closed-circuit response ratios, not open-loop stability margins.
The iterative pole search hit its limit. Its partial pole list cannot establish stability.
nextQuestion: Review the second gate operating-state branch and small-signal response, beyond endpoint current fitting, against independently supported device behavior.

baseline.scope: Closed BR1 and complete reference oscillator including unused gate and reference CPU load. Unit AC current injects into OSC_RC; DC injection is zero. Ratios are loaded responses within the closed circuit, not open-loop gain, stability margins or a startup proof. Observed external-node plateau agreement does not prove identical internal junction states. Frequency coverage and generic device parameters do not establish physical bandwidth.
